svg.title: MN 43 Mahāvedalla Sutta — The Greater Series of Questions and Answers
svg.desc: A discourse visualization of MN 43: wisdom measured against the four noble truths; consciousness, felt experience and perception named by what each does and found only together; the purified mind-consciousness released from the five faculties; the two conditions and five supports of right view; the three realms of existence; the five factors given up and five present in the first jhāna; the five faculties resting on mind and on the mutual dependence of vitality and body heat, shown by the flame and radiance of a burning oil lamp; the vital formations distinguishing death from the cessation of perception and what is felt; and the four releases of mind culminating in the unshakeable release, empty of passion, aversion and delusion.

g.text: The Greater Series of Questions and Answers
A series of questions and answers between venerable Sāriputta and venerable Mahākoṭṭhita
that clarify subtle yet important aspects of the teachings.
One who is undiscerning and one who is wise
this is the way to its ending
this is the way to its ending
These three are closely associated, not unassociated
What one experiences, that one perceives; what one perceives, that one distinguishes
yaṁ vedeti taṁ sañjānāti, yaṁ sañjānāti taṁ vijānāti
Wisdom is to be cultivated, and consciousness is to be completely comprehended
released from the five faculties — nissaṭṭhena pañcahi indriyehi
A quality that can be known is discerned through the eye of wisdom
neyyaṁ kho, āvuso, dhammaṁ paññācakkhunā pajānāti
for the sake of direct knowledge
for the sake of complete comprehension
for the sake of letting go
two conditions bring right view to be; five factors support it; two fruits follow from it
SUPPORTED BY FIVE FACTORS · PAÑCAHAṄGEHI ANUGGAHITĀ
three realms of existence — tayome bhavā
Production of renewed existence occurs from
Thorough enjoyment of this and that
Renewed existence does not occur from
five factors given up, five factors present — pañcaṅgavippahīnaṁ, pañcaṅgasamannāgataṁ
Secluded from sensual pleasures and unwholesome states — born of seclusion, and imbued with uplifting joy and pleasure
vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṁ savicāraṁ vivekajaṁ pītisukhaṁ paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati
each with its own field and domain, experiencing no other's — nānāvisayāni nānāgocarāni
The five faculties stand dependent on vitality; vitality on body heat; and body heat on vitality
pañcindriyāni āyuṁ paṭicca tiṭṭhanti · āyu usmaṁ paṭicca tiṭṭhati · usmā āyuṁ paṭicca tiṭṭhati
seen as the lamp's radiance · ābhā
seen as the lamp's flame · acci
telappadīpassa jhāyato acciṁ paṭicca ābhā paññāyati, ābhaṁ paṭicca acci paññāyati
what sustains a life is not what is felt — and so cessation is not death
Vital formations are not things that can be felt
Na teva āyusaṅkhārā te vedaniyā dhammā
WHEN THREE THINGS LEAVE THIS BODY
— it lies discarded, senseless as a log · yathā kaṭṭhaṁ acetanaṁ
One in the cessation of perception and what is felt
alike in their constructs; unalike in vitality, heat, and faculties
releases that differ in expression — and one that they all point to
pleasure and pain given up · mental pleasure
in one respect different in meaning and in expression; in another, the same in meaning and different only in expression
empty of self and anything pertaining to a self
WHY THEY ARE ONE IN MEANING
abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump · pahīnā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā
empty of passion, empty of aversion, empty of delusion — suññā rāgena, suññā dosena, suññā mohena
